newsitem.title: INDIA: GOLD - Indian sub-continent prices seen falling.
newsitem.headline: GOLD - Indian sub-continent prices seen falling.

text.p: Poor seasonal demand in India and Pakistan is likely to push gold prices further down in the Indian sub-continent in the current week, dealers said on Monday.
They said subdued demand in the Indian sub-continent would also depress bullion trade in Dubai, the re-export market for gold into India and Pakistan.
Prices had generally been subdued in the Indian sub-continent and in Dubai in the week to Monday.
"The peak marriage season in India is now over and we are witnessing poor demand," said Babubhai Jain, a leading dealer on the Bombay bullion exchange.
India, the world's largest consumer of gold, imports around 300 tonnes every year and its demand peaks during the February-May wedding season.
In Bombay, standard gold (24 carats) fell 25 rupees to 4,770 rupees per 10 grammes in the week to Monday.
A subdued trend in the world market had also affected sentiment on the Indian market, dealers said.
"The short-term outlook is likely to be subdued and prices may move in a narrow range but the long-term trend depends on the monsoon factor," said Mahavir Shah, a leading jeweller.
India, a predominently agricultural country, largely depends on the four-month June-September monsoon season for the growth of its crops.
"If the monsoon starts on time, gold will witness higher rural demand. But a delay in its arrival can affect market sentiment," Shah said.
In Karachi, Pakistan's main commercial city, gold prices are likely to remain mixed in the current week on low demand because of a shortage of funds, dealers said.
In Dubai, the trading hub of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), bullion dealers reported a dull trend in the week to Sunday, attributing it to scant demand from India and Pakistan.
"The market is very, very dull. There is no physical demand from India or Pakistan," said one trader.

"Muharram is still going on and there is no (wedding or festival) season in India at the moment," he added, referring to the Moslem Muharram period which is a traditionally slow time for retail business.
"The outlook is also pretty bleak. The international market is weak and there is no bullish news around to pull it higher," said another dealer.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES in U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion $1=35.76 Indian rupees, 40.49 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams)
*Bombay prices May 26/19, Karachi and Dubai May 25/18
